deck: 30 Thinking in Java::02 Everything Is an Object

cards.front: When you write String s;, what have you actually created?
cards.extra: The book's television/remote model: the reference can exist with no television attached. Sending a message to it then fails at runtime, not at compile time.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: What happens if you call a method on a reference that was never attached to an object?
cards.extra: The compiler cannot tell whether the remote is pointed at anything, so s.length() compiles and then fails when the program runs.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: Why can a String be written as a quoted literal when other objects cannot?
cards.back: Strings are a special case: the compiler builds the object for you
cards.extra: String s = "asdf"; is legal shorthand; every other type needs new. The quotes create the object, not just a reference.

cards.front: Do primitives work by reference too?
cards.back: No — a primitive variable holds the value itself
cards.extra: That is why int a = 5; int b = a; gives two independent numbers, while assigning one object variable to another gives two references to one object.

cards.front: In Thinking in Java's framing, what does static mean?
cards.back: The member exists independently of any object — one per class
cards.extra: A static field is shared by every instance and reachable through the class name. A static method can be called without constructing anything.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::04 Static Keyword

cards.front: What do fields get if you never initialise them?
cards.extra: The book uses this to contrast fields with locals: locals must be assigned before use, fields never are.

cards.back: A new scope: names declared inside are invisible outside
cards.extra: Scoping is lexical, decided by braces. That is why a variable declared inside a loop body cannot be used after the loop.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: A method creates an object inside a block and the block ends. Does the object die?
cards.back: No — only the reference dies; the object lives on the heap
cards.extra: Scope governs names, not lifetimes. The object stays until nothing references it, which is the whole reason the garbage collector exists.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::20 Pass by Value vs Pass by Reference
